newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum Association tight-lipped on USTR talks.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum Association tight-lipped on USTR talks.

text.p: The Aluminum Association was tight-lipped following talks with "appropriate officials" at the United States Trade Representative in Washington on Wednesday, saying the next move was up to the Administration.

Barry Meyer, Aluminum Association's vice-president of government relations, said the talks with USTR centered on eliminating the European Union's 8.5 percent tariff on imports of aluminum mill products.
Other topics were discussed but Meyer declined to elaborate or indicate the tone of the meeting.
"We have a longstanding position of wanting tariffs on aluminum worldwide to be reduced to zero, which is U.S. government policy," Meyer said.
The Aluminum Association, which groups U.S. primary and secondary producers, has lobbied the government to press for zero tariffs in Europe many times, Meyer added.
"Everything is in the government's court," Meyer said.
Aluminum producers elsewhere in the world have also been engaged in a long-running campaign to reduce or eliminate the EU tariff.
There are no tariffs on aluminum imported from the EU into the U.S.
In the past the Aluminum Association has tried to persuade USTR to raise the tariff issue at relevant international trade forums.
